## Overview of findings
### Key takeaways
- Build single-leg control and a strength base
- Add velocity through the lower half: drive, stride and hip rotation

### Strengths
- **Fastball velocity is climbing: 60.8 mph.** Latest session PitchLogic · 2026-09-19 averaged 60.8 mph vs 59.6 mph across the previous 2 (+1.2 mph); top 61.5 mph. Normal session-to-session variation here is about ±0.3 mph.

### Notes
- **No health clearance on file.** Record a health assessment so the plan can account for clearance, pain and arm soreness.
- **4D Motion capture on file.** 4D Motion · 2026-09-19: Pelvis/Chest - Peak Closing Separation 81.2 , Chest - Peak Opening Rotation -22 . Recapture after this block to compare sequencing against her own baseline.
- **No movement screen yet.** The weight room program starts with Foundational strength until a movement screen is recorded.
- **1 active goal.** "Add 2 mph to my fastball"

### Root cause: why each finding fired
- **Fastball velocity is climbing: 60.8 mph:** Change of 0.5 mph or more vs. the previous sessions, and larger than normal variation (2 standard errors)

## Pitching program
4-week off-season block, 3 pitching days per week. Pitch counts are ranges for the whole session including warm-up pitches.

### Week 1: Settle in: moderate volume, sharp mechanics
- **Day 1, Drill work (21-30 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (34-47 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Rise ball, Changeup.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (26-34 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Week 2: Build: a little more volume and intent
- **Day 1, Drill work (24-33 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (38-52 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Rise ball, Changeup.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (29-38 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Week 3: Build: a little more volume and intent
- **Day 1, Drill work (26-37 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (42-58 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Rise ball, Changeup.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (32-42 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Week 4: Deload: lighter week to absorb the work
- **Day 1, Drill work (18-25 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Walk-throughs and step-through drills: hips lead, arm follows. Drive-leg push-off and stride-length marker drills (stride direction to the plate). Film one set and compare against the 4D Motion capture sequencing.
- **Day 2, Bullpen (28-39 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. About half the pitches at full intent with PitchLogic speed feedback after each pitch; rest 20-30 s between. Mix: Fastball, Rise ball, Changeup.
- **Day 3, Spin and movement (21-28 pitches):** Warm-up: arm circles, band work, progressive catch to full distance. Spin drills on each pitch type; note spin rate and direction on PitchLogic.

### Rules for the block
- Estimated age 17 from graduation year 2027: STOP Sports Injuries recommendations cap a game day at 100 pitches for this age.
- No more than 3 pitching days in a row, then rest (STOP Sports Injuries guideline for 13 and over).
- Stop the session at any pain and tell the coach.
- Games count toward the week: a game replaces the nearest bullpen.
- Re-check in PitchLogic at the end of the block: average and top velocity, total spin and vertical movement.

## Weight room program
**Main program: Foundational strength and control.** Build the base: single-leg control, hinge and squat patterns, trunk stiffness and shoulder durability before chasing power.
- No movement screen yet: Foundational strength first.
- Arm care is part of every pitcher's week.

### Foundation: Day A (Lower body and anti-rotation)
Warm-up: 5 min easy movement, then 90/90 hip switches x 6, world's greatest stretch x 3 each side, band pull-aparts x 15.
- Goblet box squat: 3 x 8 at RPE 6-7 (Knees track over toes, sit back to the box)
- Split squat (bodyweight or light dumbbells): 3 x 8 each at RPE 6-7 (Front knee stays stacked, no inward collapse)
- Dumbbell Romanian deadlift: 3 x 10 at RPE 6-7
- Pallof press: 3 x 10 each side (Ribs down, resist the rotation)
- Side plank: 2 x 20-30 s each

### Foundation: Day B (Upper body pull, single-leg balance, arm care)
Warm-up: Band external rotation x 15, band Y-T-W x 8 each, wall slides x 10.
- Single-leg Romanian deadlift (reach): 3 x 8 each at RPE 6 (Slow, hips square)
- Half-kneeling one-arm dumbbell row: 3 x 10 each at RPE 7
- Push-up (incline if needed): 3 x 8-12 at RPE 7
- Lateral band walk: 2 x 12 steps each way
- Prone Y and T raise: 2 x 10 each
- Dead bug: 3 x 8 each side

Progression: Week to week add 1-2 reps per set until the top of the range, then add load and drop back to the bottom of the range. Every fourth week, cut sets by a third.

### Add-on: Arm care and scapular durability
Arm care (10-15 min, most days).
- Band external rotation at 0° and 90°: 2 x 15 each
- Prone Y-T-W: 2 x 8 each
- Serratus wall slide with lift-off: 2 x 10
- Half-kneeling band row to external rotation: 2 x 10 each
- Eccentric biceps curl (light, slow 4 s lower): 2 x 8 each
- Sleeper or cross-body stretch (only if cleared by the clinician): 2 x 30 s

### Weekly schedule
- **Week 1** (RPE at the low end of each range): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 2** (Progress per the program's rule): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 3** (Progress per the program's rule): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B
- **Week 4** (Deload: cut sets by a third, keep technique crisp): Foundation Day A, Foundation Day B

### Cautions
- Move to Lower-half power only once single-leg squats hold alignment for all reps.
- Any shoulder or elbow pain during arm care: stop and tell the coach.
- Internal-rotation deficits are flagged for the clinician; the stretch is included only with their okay.

## Why this plan
Triggers that fired:
- Fastball velocity is climbing: 60.8 mph: Change of 0.5 mph or more vs. the previous sessions, and larger than normal variation (2 standard errors)

Research behind it:
- STOP Sports Injuries / AOSSM fastpitch pitching recommendations, as summarized in Kamarajugadda et al., Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine, 2023: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10226313/
- Friesen et al., Orthopaedic Journal of Sports Medicine, 2021: https://doi.org/10.1177/2325967121990920
- NSCA Youth Resistance Training position statement: https://www.nsca.com/globalassets/about/position-statements/position_stand_youth_resistance_training---2009.pdf
- Shanley et al., American Journal of Sports Medicine, 2011: https://doi.org/10.1177/0363546511408876
- Rojas et al., American Journal of Sports Medicine, 2009: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/23953920_Biceps_Activity_During_Windmill_Softball_Pitching_Injury_Implications_and_Comparison_With_Overhand_Throwing
- Guy et al., International Journal of Sports Physical Therapy, 2021: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8637248/
